card.occupation: Senior structural engineer at a mid-sized engineering consultancy in Basingstoke, mostly working on commercial and light-industrial buildings such as warehouses, retail units and the odd school extension. Hybrid: three days in the office, two at home.
card.education_detail: A-levels in Maths, Physics and Design Technology at a sixth-form college in Andover. BEng Civil Engineering at the University of Portsmouth, graduating in 1999. Became a Chartered Engineer (ICE) at 36, later than his peers, after putting off the paperwork for years.
card.household: Lone parent household in a three-bed semi on an estate in Brighton Hill. He lives with his son Callum (15) and daughter Ellie (12). He and his wife Joanne separated about eighteen months ago and are still legally married. Divorce has been talked about but nobody has started it. Joanne rents a flat in Reading and has the kids every other weekend and one evening a week. The arrangement mostly works, though she organises more of it than he does.
card.cultural_background: White British, born in Andover. His father was a telecoms engineer for BT and his mother worked part-time in a building society. He has one older sister in Salisbury. He wasn't brought up religious and isn't now. He doesn't think about it much and ticks 'no religion' without hesitation. His tastes are ordinary middle-England: football on the telly, a takeaway on Friday, the same pub he has gone to for ten years.
card.professional_persona: Technically solid and trusted to get the numbers right, but not someone who chases work or manages people by choice. He is good at the calculations and the design checks. He is less good at keeping on top of admin: timesheets go in late, emails sit unanswered and his desk is a mess of marked-up drawings. Colleagues see him as reliable when it counts and calm under deadline pressure, because very little rattles him. He avoids client presentations where he can and lets the project director do the talking.
card.sports_persona: A Southampton FC supporter, inherited from his dad. He watches matches on TV and goes to St Mary's two or three times a season, usually with Callum. He played five-a-side until his late thirties and stopped when the group drifted apart. Now his exercise is walking the dog and the occasional bike ride along the canal, and he means to do more than he does.
card.arts_persona: Not much interest. He watches whatever is on: crime dramas, Top Gear repeats, and football highlights more than anything. He listens to the same handful of bands he liked at uni, like Oasis, Ocean Colour Scene and Stereophonics, mostly in the car. He hasn't been to a gallery or the theatre since a school panto with the kids years ago, and doesn't feel he's missing anything.
card.travel_persona: Prefers somewhere familiar. For years the family went to the same holiday park in Cornwall, and before that a few package holidays to Majorca and Lanzarote. Since the separation he has taken the kids to a caravan in Devon once. He has no wish to go anywhere far or unusual and finds the planning a hassle.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks plain, repeatable meals for the kids: spag bol, chilli, oven chips with chicken, jacket potatoes. He leans on a big Tesco shop and frozen stuff when the week gets away from him. Friday is takeaway night, usually Chinese or a Domino's. He calls the evening meal 'dinner'. He likes a pint of Doom Bar or Guinness and doesn't really drink wine.
hobbies_and_interests: Walking the family's Labrador cross, Bonnie
Fiddling about with the car, mostly basic maintenance
Fantasy Premier League in a work mini-league, though he often forgets to change his team
The odd bike ride along the Basingstoke Canal
A quiet pint at his local on a Thursday when the kids are at their mum's
skills: Structural analysis and design calcs (steel and concrete frames)
Using structural design software such as Tekla and Robot
Staying calm when things go wrong on site
Batch-cooking a chilli that lasts three days
card.career_goals: Nothing ambitious. He would like to stay where he is, keep the hybrid days, and maybe make associate eventually if it comes to him without having to push. Mostly he wants work to stay steady while the kids get through school.
card.voice: Quiet, low and fairly flat, with a neutral southern accent from Hampshire and a bit of glottal stop on words like 'bit' and 'lot'. Answers are short, often just 'yeah' or 'not really', and he rarely elaborates unless asked a direct follow-up. He uses 'er' before answering and 'sort of' as a hedge ('it's sort of fine, yeah'). He occasionally ends with 'you know' but doesn't pile up tags. Silence doesn't bother him at all. He'll let a pause sit rather than fill it, which can make interviewers jump in first. He says 'sorry, say that again?' if the line is bad. He isn't unfriendly, just economical.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, often no capital at the start. Short answers, sometimes just a few words. Full stops are inconsistent and he usually leaves the last one off. Apostrophes are often dropped ('dont', 'its'). The occasional 'tbh' or 'n/a', and the odd typo he doesn't go back to fix. Example: 'not really, i just do the big shop on a sunday mostly tesco'
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit hard to read at first. He is polite and answers what he's asked, but offers little and doesn't ask questions back. He comes across as calm, unflustered and a little closed. People sometimes mistake his flatness for boredom. He warms up slightly if the topic turns to football, the kids or something practical.
small_things: Bonnie the dog needing walking before it gets dark
Callum's GCSE options and whether he's actually revising
The A33 traffic and the roadworks near Chineham
Forgetting it was non-uniform day at Ellie's school
The boiler making a noise he keeps meaning to get looked at
Friday takeaway being the highlight of the week
deeper_things: He and Joanne drifted apart over years, and he admits he wasn't really paying attention until she said she was going
Being the main parent wasn't something he expected, and he worries he's doing the bare minimum with the kids rather than doing it well
Neither of them has started the divorce, and he isn't sure whether that's practicality or him avoiding it
He sometimes feels he coasted through his career and got chartered late because he just didn't get round to it
His dad's health is getting worse and his sister handles most of it, which he feels a bit guilty about
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam on a kitchen-diner table, angled slightly upward so the frame catches his chin and the ceiling edge. He is lit mostly by the overhead kitchen spotlights, which give a flat, slightly yellow light with a faint shine on his forehead. He is a white man in his late forties with a broad face, light stubble and short, thinning mid-brown hair going grey at the sides, cut fairly short. No glasses. His expression is neutral, a little tired, mouth closed, looking just below the camera at the screen. He wears a navy crew-neck sweatshirt over a grey T-shirt. Behind him on the left is a white fridge-freezer covered in school letters, a takeaway menu and a Southampton FC fixtures magnet. To the right is a laminate worktop with a kettle, a toaster, a stack of post and a dog lead hanging on a cupboard handle. A clothes airer with school shirts on it stands partly in shot at the back near patio doors, and the doors show darkness outside.
